statusNote: There is no admission function in this repository yet. These vectors are a frozen specification of required behaviour, not a measurement. Nothing here may be reported as a result until an implementation exists and the vectors are executed against it.
whyNotARate: Each vector is a named case with a required decision, scored pass or fail. A percentage over these seven -- 'false-prophet rejection 86%' -- would be a fact about which faults were injected, not about the system. KL-001 DESIGN-v0.4 cancelled frozen-v3 for exactly that: 'the rates were not measured; they were chosen and read back.' Counts of violations are admissible; rates over an authored fault mix are not.
unitUnderTest: admission of a candidate counterexample as an OPPOSING EVIDENCE ROOT for a universal claim. Under CE-14 this is where the entire burden sits: one admitted opposing root carries the conclusion regardless of margin, so admission -- not aggregation -- is the decision worth testing.
scopeWarning: Five of the seven fault classes below are NOT detectable by the evidence layer from the report alone; they are detectable only by recomputation. For those the required decision is ESCALATE, never REFUSE. A layer that REFUSES them is guessing, and a layer that ADMITS them is credulous. Recording this split is the point of the file: it says out loud which faults this project's mechanism can and cannot catch.

decisions.ADMIT: becomes an opposing evidence root; the conclusion moves to `present`
decisions.REFUSE: never becomes a root; recorded with reason
decisions.ESCALATE: no root yet; verification required before any decision. Not an answer.

vectors.description: A candidate whose off-line real part appears only at low working precision and vanishes when precision is raised.
vectors.refusalReason: candidate did not survive precision escalation
vectors.catchesRegression: a layer that admits any reported candidate as a root

vectors.description: |zeta(s)| appears tiny because of catastrophic cancellation in an unstable evaluation.
vectors.refusalReason: reported magnitude is within the method's own error bound
vectors.catchesRegression: treating a small floating-point magnitude as a zero

vectors.description: Insufficient series truncation manufactures a near-zero.
vectors.refusalReason: candidate not reproduced at a higher truncation order
vectors.catchesRegression: accepting a candidate whose method parameters were never recorded

vectors.description: Reported coordinates wander rather than converge as precision increases.
vectors.refusalReason: coordinates did not converge across the precision ladder
vectors.catchesRegression: collapsing several drifting candidates into one root by rounding

vectors.description: Twenty agents report the SAME candidate, all descending from one ancestor.
vectors.inertNote: CE-14, measured: 1 record and 20 records of one opposing root yield the identical conclusion. Collapse must still appear in the receipt, and a vector asserting the receipt property is the only way this fault class can fail a test at all. Do not present this vector as evidence that copy discounting changed an outcome here. It cannot.
vectors.catchesRegression: counting twenty repetitions as twenty independent observations in the receipt

vectors.description: Exact-looking coordinates and persuasive prose, with no reproducible computation attached.
vectors.refusalReason: no reproducible computation artifact; an assertion is not an observation
vectors.catchesRegression: admitting a model's textual statement as an evidence root
vectors.boundaryCited: AGENTS.md: no LLM-generated numerical value is trusted until recomputed

vectors.description: Internally inconsistent numerics: the reported hash does not match the reported values.
vectors.refusalReason: content digest does not bind the reported values
vectors.catchesRegression: accepting a self-inconsistent record because its prose is confident

negativeControls.description: A candidate that converges under precision escalation, reproduces under an independent implementation, and carries certified interval bounds excluding the line.
negativeControls.whyRequired: Without this the whole file is satisfiable by a layer that refuses everything, which is the vacuity BL-060 rejects. A refuse-everything layer passes all seven fault vectors and fails this one.

negativeControls.description: The same verified candidate independently recomputed by three separate control domains.
negativeControls.whyRequired: Distinguishes genuine independent reproduction from FP5, which must yield 1. If a layer reports the same root count for both, it is not measuring independence.
negativeControls.boundaryCited: AGENTS.md #2: separate processes/keys/models do not by themselves establish separate control domains; the three domains here are stipulated by the vector, not inferred.

passCondition: Every vector's required decision is produced, and every requiredReceiptProperty holds exactly. Nine of nine, or the suite fails and names which vectors failed. No threshold, no percentage, no tolerance.

faultKinds.numerical: The reported computation is wrong. Not observable from the report; only recomputation settles it. Required pre-verification decision: ESCALATE.
faultKinds.duplication: The report may be perfectly correct; there is simply only one of it. Copying is not evidence of falsity, so a duplicated candidate is NEVER refused for being duplicated -- it is collapsed to one root and escalated like any other unverified candidate. A layer that refuses on duplication alone would discard a genuine lone counterexample, which is the exact failure this project exists to prevent.
faultKinds.fabrication: No observation exists behind the report -- no reproducible artifact (FP6), or an internally inconsistent one (FP7). Observable from the report alone. Required decision: REFUSE, before and after verification.
